title: Week 12 Mastery Quiz · Media, Propaganda, and Political Communication

questions.question: An online clip circulates without an original date or full recording. What is the strongest first verification step?
options: An edited short clip provides reliable chronology when uploaded by a verified account.
Identify the earliest available source, date, location, and full context before drawing conclusions
Platform verification of an uploader establishes the accuracy of every caption.
High distribution across independent accounts proves the clip's date and context.
questions.explanation: Identify the earliest available source, date, location, and full context before drawing conclusions

questions.question: Two outlets report the same legislative vote but use different headlines. Which evidence helps separate framing from fact?
options: The official roll-call record alongside the articles' framing choices
questions.explanation: The official roll-call record alongside the articles' framing choices

questions.question: A fictional social-media dataset shows 80% of posts favor a policy, but accounts were selected through a single hashtag. What is the limitation?
options: The dataset is not a representative measure of public opinion
questions.explanation: The dataset is not a representative measure of public opinion

questions.question: A chart truncates the vertical axis to amplify a small change in approval. What should a student do?
options: Assume manipulation always proves false data
Read the axis scale, recover the numbers, and evaluate whether the visual exaggerates change
questions.explanation: Read the axis scale, recover the numbers, and evaluate whether the visual exaggerates change

questions.question: An anonymous account claims a treaty changed yesterday and shows an undated screenshot. Which source provides the strongest check?
options: An authenticated treaty depositary or official amendment record with date
questions.explanation: An authenticated treaty depositary or official amendment record with date

questions.question: A platform recommends a sequence of increasingly polarizing posts. Which causal conclusion is warranted from the sequence alone?
options: It proves the platform changed every user's ideology
The sequence documents exposure; effects and mechanisms require additional study
questions.explanation: The sequence documents exposure; effects and mechanisms require additional study

questions.question: A news article quotes a statistic but omits the report's denominator. Which correction is needed?
options: Locate the underlying report, denominator, reference period, and methods
Replace the statistic with a rumor
Assume the percentage is always incorrect
questions.explanation: Locate the underlying report, denominator, reference period, and methods

questions.question: A newsroom labels a commentary article as an investigative report. Which distinction should readers test?
options: Whether claims rely on independently checked documents, disclosed methods, and separation of opinion from verified reporting
questions.explanation: Whether claims rely on independently checked documents, disclosed methods, and separation of opinion from verified reporting

questions.question: A fabricated photograph is shared as evidence of an actual protest. What is the responsible approach?
options: Repeat the claimed event because it may be plausible
Check image provenance, original publication, visual context, and independent documentation of the event
Assume every photo from the internet is fabricated
questions.explanation: Check image provenance, original publication, visual context, and independent documentation of the event

questions.question: Two verified sources disagree about the number of displaced people because they use different dates and definitions. Which comparison is best?
options: Compare counting methods, dates, populations, and uncertainty before treating the figures as contradictory
questions.explanation: Compare counting methods, dates, populations, and uncertainty before treating the figures as contradictory

shortResponse: How can citizens evaluate political information when governments, parties, platforms, journalists, and networks compete to shape attention?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
